adherence.reason: Uses a magical clay golem and a threatened city in a fantasy setting.
The narrator is a clay golem protector, but neither a rabbi creator nor a besieged ghetto is stated.
Later passages use first person, but the opening two sentences describe the golem in third person.
It explicitly says the golem stood sentinel each night at the cliffside gates.
The gates are cliffside, but the city itself is not clearly built into the cliff.
The golem understands the child's question and speaks, rather than only sensing intentions and fear.
The story contains substantially more than six sentences.
It has watched for two hundred years without a command, but does not establish that everyone it knew died or that no stop command was omitted.
It first speaks to a child, but the child is not said not to run away and the ending is not precisely this event.
A supernatural clay guardian and magical setting make this fantasy.
The first-person golem says it was crafted under a rabbi's watch during ghetto strife.
The narration is consistently voiced as the golem's first-person account.
The golem explicitly begins a vigil at Ghetto Hollow's gates each night.
Cliffside streets and chasms are present, but the city being built into the cliff is only implied.
It initially says words have no meaning and it knows intentions and fear, but later claims to understand human complexity.
The response has far more than six sentences.
It explicitly says two hundred years passed, everyone it knew died, and it received no command ending its watch.
A child who does not flee prompts its first word, but further narration follows the spoken word.
